page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-16 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, positioning it within the memory-optimized resource tier. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent disk operations.

The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance without the resource contention typical of shared-core or burstable instances. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density per vCPU makes this instance type suitable for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without the added expense of scaling up the vCPU count. It does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which should be factored into network architecture planning.

Given the 128 GB memory capacity and dedicated compute resources, the n4d-highmem-16 is designed for memory-intensive applications. Appropriate workloads include medium-sized databases, in-memory caching layers, enterprise applications, and data processing pipelines that require significant RAM but do not demand specialized GPU acceleration or high-speed local NVMe storage.
